newsitem.title: GERMANY: German funds group warns against share tax plan.
newsitem.headline: German funds group warns against share tax plan.

text.p: The German association of investment companies (BVI) on Friday warned that a controversial proposal to impose capital gains tax on stock investments would weaken Germany as a financial centre.

BVI said the plans put forward by the CDU, the minor party in Germany's ruling coalition, would clash with efforts to promote an equity culture in Germany, especially given the gigantic imminent flotation of Deutsche Telekom.

Current German laws exempt shares from capital gains tax as long as gains are not realised for at least six months, but a recent CDU policy document mooted removing that exemption as part of broad tax reform.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel, of the dominant CSU party, has since said the idea needed further examination.

"A general imposition of tax on share capital gains would deal a significant blow to the readiness of a broader investor group to invest in shares, which has just recently developed," the BVI said in a statement.
"It would also undermine efforts to improve the capital set-up of newer companies," the association added.
The BVI also cautioned that the move to tax share gains could provoke flight of capital.

If the tax move does go ahead, rates of taxation should be reduced and exemptions granted for longer term investments. Another option would be to exempt share capital gains which are directly reinvested, the BVI suggested.
Talk of the tax has already unsettled stock market analysts here, who also fear it could derail efforts to promote the stock market in a traditionally risk averse climate.
The imminent Deutsche Telekom flotation, scheduled for late November, is viewed as an ideal chance to woo first-time investors and has attracted unprecedented interest.
